claims.evidence: NHS page: do not take in pregnancy unless advised by a doctor or pharmacist (seen). 'Withdrawal symptoms in the baby' was NOT found on the NHS diazepam page; it appears in the manufacturer patient leaflet (medicines.org.uk): 'if taken regularly during pregnancy your baby may develop withdrawal symptoms'. Attribution wrong.
claims.newSentence: The NHS says diazepam should not be taken in pregnancy unless a doctor or pharmacist advises it. The manufacturer's patient leaflet says that if it is taken regularly during pregnancy, the baby may develop withdrawal symptoms.

notes: Only search summaries were available (no page fetch). Human check: (1) NHS diazepam pregnancy text re baby withdrawal; (2) 'rare' qualifier on serious side effects; (3) the 'up to 4 weeks' wording was seen in NHS summary but sentences omit the number (fine); (4) driving: only NHS advice checked, not DVLA/drug-driving law; (5) index 32 gives 999/NHS 111 for severe withdrawal, not in sources - keep calm and consider rewording; (6) Class C under the 1971 Act seen only via ACMD, not Schedule 2 of the Act itself; (7) several 'excerpt' basis labels are search summaries not verbatim quotes; (8) MHRA page also gives taper schedules - correctly NOT used (no dosing). Medication index 7 and class index 0 tail are site statements, not facts. | Editorial tidy-ups after the second pass (duplicate sentences removed or one wording softened) are marked in the claims where they apply. Replacement sentences came from the second-pass retrieval and were not run through a third check.
